speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin assessing your symptoms of agitation and yellowing of the skin and eyes, have you noticed any darkening of your urine or lightening of your stools recently? Also, have you experienced any abdominal pain, particularly in the upper right side?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, have you had any recent unprotected sexual encounters or shared needles? I also need to know if you are currently taking any prescription medications or herbal supplements.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any fever, nausea, or loss of appetite before the jaundice and agitation started? I will also check for any signs of liver tenderness or encephalopathy during my physical exam. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly reduced prothrombin activity and elevated INR indicate acute liver failure, which explains your agitation. To determine the cause, I need to know if you have had any recent unprotected sexual contact with a new partner, and have you noticed any right upper quadrant abdominal pain or tenderness? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the hepatitis panel is normal, I need to rule out other causes of acute liver failure. Have you taken any acetaminophen or used any herbal supplements recently? I will also check for signs of autoimmune hepatitis or Wilson's disease. REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral hepatitis and acetaminophen toxicity ruled out, I need to evaluate for Wilson's disease or other metabolic causes. Have you noticed any tremors, psychiatric changes other than agitation, or a family history of liver disease? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Copper_Ceruloplasmin

speaker: Doctor
text: Since common causes like viral hepatitis, acetaminophen, and Wilson's disease are ruled out, I need to consider ischemic hepatitis or drug-induced liver injury. Have you experienced any recent episodes of severe hypotension, shock, or heart failure? Also, given your history of ecstasy use, did you take any new recreational drugs or supplements in the last two weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of ecstasy use and acute liver failure with normal viral and metabolic workups, I suspect toxic hepatitis from a contaminant in the recreational drugs. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Acetaminophen_Level_and_Ecstasy_Metabolites

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of ecstasy metabolites confirms that your acute liver failure is due to MDMA toxicity. DIAGNOSIS READY: MDMA-induced acute liver failure
